annotations.description: Mulliganed a 2-land mono-white hand with an excellent spell curve (3-drop, 3-drop, 4-drop, 4-drop, plus a combat trick). In a mono-colored limited deck, 2 lands is on the low end but keepable - you have ~55-60% chance to draw a third land by turn 3, and all your spells are high quality. Going to 6 cards loses card advantage and doesn't guarantee a better hand.
annotations.betterLine: Keep the 7-card hand. Two Plains with an excellent mono-white curve is a reasonable keep, accepting the risk of missing the third land drop in exchange for card advantage and hand quality.

annotations.description: Player timed out on the Thriving Heath color choice, which is a permanent and irreversible mana decision. The default was likely assigned (probably Blue), but without knowing their deck's second color, there's roughly a 75% chance this was the wrong color. In a Limited deck, having the wrong color on your dual land can be meaningfully costly throughout the game.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out, allowing the game to assign a default color (likely Blue) for Thriving Heath.
annotations.betterLine: Actively choose the color matching their deck's second color to ensure Thriving Heath provides the correct mana fixing for the rest of the game.

annotations.description: Player passed with 2 untapped mana and no other plays available this turn or at instant speed. The Clue token could be cracked for free (no opportunity cost) to draw a card, potentially finding a 2-drop or improving future draws.

annotations.betterLine: Activate the Clue token to draw a card, since there are no instants in hand and no other way to use the 2 mana this turn cycle.

annotations.description: The opponent has no available blockers (Basri's Acolyte is summoning sick, Guardian Idol is tapped), so both Thraben Inspector and Inspiring Overseer could attack for free. Attacking with only the Overseer leaves 1 damage on the table for no clear benefit.

annotations.betterLine: Attack with both Inspiring Overseer and Thraben Inspector for 3 total damage, since the opponent has zero available blockers. With Inspiring Unicorn and upcoming Valorous Steed available as blockers, holding back the 1/2 Inspector is unnecessary.

annotations.description: Gem3P Coach declined to attack with Basri's Acolyte (2/3 lifelink) when the opponent's only untapped creature was Thraben Inspector (1/2) and all opponent lands were tapped, meaning no combat tricks. Attacking guarantees either killing the Inspector while gaining 2 life, or dealing 2 damage and gaining 2 life if unblocked. Both outcomes are purely positive.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to attack with Basri's Acolyte
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Basri's Acolyte. It favorably trades with or tramples over the 1/2 Inspector, gaining life in the process, with zero risk since opponent has no mana available.

annotations.description: Passed priority in precombat main phase with a land drop available, 4 untapped lands, and the opponent completely tapped out. Could play Plains (5 lands) then cast Faith's Fetters on Basri's Acolyte to permanently neutralize it and gain 4 life, or at minimum cast Brightmare to tap Basri's Acolyte before attacking. Passing here ends the main phase and wastes the entire turn's development.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority with no action, skipping the precombat main phase entirely.
annotations.betterLine: Play Plains (5 lands), then cast Faith's Fetters targeting Basri's Acolyte to neutralize it and gain 4 life, then attack with Inspiring Unicorn, Inspiring Overseer, and Thraben Inspector into an opponent with no untapped blockers except Mesa Unicorn (which is sick).

annotations.description: Only attacked with Inspiring Overseer (2 damage) when the opponent had only Basri's Acolyte 2/3 as a blocker (Mesa Unicorn sick, Guardian Idol tapped). Attacking with all three creatures would trigger Inspiring Unicorn's +1/+1 buff, letting the flying Overseer deal 3, and forcing the Acolyte to block just one ground creature - resulting in 6-7 damage total and likely trading off the Acolyte. GPT54 Sport also had Valorous Stance in hand as combat trick protection.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only Inspiring Overseer for 2 damage.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with all three creatures (Inspiring Overseer, Inspiring Unicorn, Thraben Inspector). Inspiring Unicorn's trigger buffs all attackers to 3/2, 3/3, and 2/3. The opponent can only block one ground creature with Basri's Acolyte, likely resulting in 6-7 damage and killing the Acolyte. Valorous Stance available as backup.

annotations.description: Attacked with only Basri's Acolyte when the opponent had all lands tapped (no combat tricks possible). Attacking with both Basri's Acolyte and Mesa Unicorn would likely gain 4+ life (triggering Griffin Aerie for a 2/2 flying token), deal more damage, and potentially force the opponent to lose Inspiring Unicorn. With only Basri's Acolyte attacking, the lifelink gain caps at 2-3, likely missing the Griffin Aerie threshold.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with both Basri's Acolyte and Mesa Unicorn into a tapped-out opponent to maximize damage, life gain, and reliably trigger Griffin Aerie

annotations.description: Gem3P Coach passed priority during their own combat phase before declaring attackers, missing the opportunity to activate Guardian Idol for 2 mana to make it a 2/2 attacker. Activating Guardian Idol would still leave 3 mana open for Feat of Resistance as a combat trick.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Guardian Idol
annotations.betterLine: Activate Guardian Idol for {2} to make it a 2/2 creature, then declare it as an attacker alongside other creatures, keeping 3 mana open for Feat of Resistance as a combat trick

annotations.betterLine: Block Basri's Acolyte with Valorous Steed (3/3). The Steed kills the 2/3 Acolyte and survives with 1 damage marked, removing a key lifelink threat that feeds Griffin Aerie.

annotations.description: Gem3P Coach only blocked with Guardian Idol when the Griffin Token (2/2) was also available to block. Despite being summoning-sick, creatures can still block.
